title: Mastering MERGE for Slowly Changing Data

scenes.line1: How do you track evolving data?
scenes.say: How do you keep track of changes in data over time? Can you use MERGE or upsert to handle this?

scenes.label: SCD
scenes.sub: Slowly Changing Dimensions track historical changes.
scenes.say: Slowly Changing Dimensions help you track historical changes in your data, keeping a record of how values evolve.
MERGE and upsert let you update existing rows or insert new ones in a single atomic step. Perfect for evolving data.

scenes.code:
MERGE INTO customers t
USING updates s ON t.id = s.id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET t.name = s.name
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, name)
VALUES (s.id, s.name);
scenes.say: Here's how a MERGE statement works. It updates matching rows and inserts new ones, all at once.

scenes.question: How do you preserve history in SCD?
scenes.right: Close out old records and insert new rows with updated values and effective dates.
scenes.say: Interviewers want more than just updates. For SCD Type 2, you need to close out old records and insert new ones with new effective dates to preserve history.
